Honoré de Balzac, The Celibates, translated by Clara Bell.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/honore-de-balzac/the-celibates/clara-bell

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Honoré de Balzac, the author, died 1851 (Wikidata Q9711). Citizenship: France.
- Clara Bell, the translator, died 1927 (Wikidata Q1091668).

First publication of the text used: 1901 (SE colophon: 'It was translated from French in 1901 by Clara Bell.' The colophon gives the original French publication as 1832 to 1842.)

Why this is public domain:
- United States: works published before 1931 are in the public domain in the United States. The colophon dates this translation to 1901. The edition's rights statement (quoted below) says the same.
- Country of origin (original French text: France; translation: not stated by the colophon): France has a term of life plus 70 years. The last person to die among the people whose words are in the text is Clara Bell, in 1927, so the text is public domain in France from 1 January 1998. The French extension for wartime does not apply, because no person in the text died after 1937. The translation's country is not stated. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life plus 70 years or less for these deaths, so the translation is public domain in each of them by 1 January 1998.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: original publication 1832 to 1842 by Honoré de Balzac; translated from French in 1901 by Clara Bell
- Wikidata Q9711 (Honoré de Balzac), death year 1851
- Wikidata Q1091668 (Clara Bell), death year 1927
